findings.text: follow-on: runs_view builds every row with _compact_row and never calls project_run_rows, so the goal's "every crew list view's rows through one projection" holds for three of the four views; the runs row's section is filled and normalized at query.py:488 by a second implementation of the rule project_run_rows owns at query.py:242-247.

follow-on: _row_state re-implements the "section declaration, falling back to the plan's status" rule that reckon/roadmap.py:1333-1345 writes inline in the same commit, so that rule now has two owners in two modules and neither extends the other.

follow-on: the fragment states that all four views "build their rows and route them through one projection", which is untrue for the runs view (reckon/crew/query.py:771), so the landed record overstates the mechanism this review exists to check.

follow-on: the baseline_suite command carries `<base-arm> ...` angle-bracket placeholders, which the manifest spec forbids ("the literal command that ran ... no angle-bracket placeholder"), so the base arm cannot be re-run from the record even though gate-base-section-state.log:3 holds the literal path.

follow-on: the done-when requires the serialized power_convertor roadmap size measured before and after "in the gate log", but this log carries only the pytest run (63 passed, EXIT=0); the size readings live in node-local scratch files that no durable path in the run directory preserves.

VERDICT goal: the goal is that every crew list view's rows pass through one projection that names each run's section; reckon/crew/query.py:221 project_run_rows is that projection and the live (query.py:327), obligations (reckon/crew/obligations.py:1383) and directory (reckon/crew/directory.py:214) views reach it, but the runs view never calls it -- runs_view builds its rows with _compact_row at reckon/crew/query.py:771 and shares only the COMMON_RUN_FIELDS constant through _selected_fields (query.py:131).
VERDICT done_when: the done-when names four clauses; tests/test_a_row_is_compact_and_names_its_section.py:187 asserts the section in all four views, :195 asserts fields=["section"] accepted by all four, :208 asserts a missing field is refused naming the fields the view has, and :319/:334 assert a done section of an in-progress plan reads its own declaration and blocks nothing; the base arm in gate-base-section-state.log records the same file at 11 failed, and the head arm records 63 passed, EXIT=0, so the gate does assert the measure.
VERDICT write_paths: the manifest's harness orientation line declares nine paths (reckon/mcp.py, reckon/crew/query.py, reckon/mcp_views.py, reckon/crew/directory.py, reckon/crew/obligations.py, reckon/roadmap.py, the test file, the evidence fragment, the figures dir) while the same run's prompt FENCE SCOPE block lists only six, omitting directory.py, obligations.py and roadmap.py; every path in the diff is inside the nine, so the two listings disagreeing is a dispatch defect rather than an overrun.
VERDICT manifest: read; status complete, negative_control_log is a bare path, and both suite fields are readable JSON (base exit 1 with 11 failing ids, head exit 0 with none), but baseline_suite.command carries `<base-arm>` angle-bracket placeholders the manifest spec forbids, so the base arm cannot be re-run from the record.

SCORE scope_discipline: 17
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: every path the diff changes (reckon/crew/query.py, reckon/crew/directory.py, reckon/crew/obligations.py, reckon/roadmap.py, reckon/mcp.py, reckon/mcp_views.py, the test file, the fragment) is inside the harness-declared write paths, and the prompt listing three fewer is an inconsistency in the dispatch rather than in the work.
SCORE durability: 18

SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: the added names follow the module's own idiom (reckon/crew/query.py:189 COMMON_RUN_FIELDS, :221 project_run_rows, reckon/mcp.py:1723 _row_state) and carry no plan, sprint or ticket identifier.

JUSTIFICATION reuse: project_run_rows extends the projection project_live_rows already owned (reckon/crew/query.py:327), but reckon/crew/query.py:488 still computes and normalizes the section for the runs row, and reckon/mcp.py:1723 _row_state re-implements the declaration-or-plan-status rule written inline at reckon/roadmap.py:1333-1345, so two owners now hold that capability.
